answers.10: Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it and inversely proportional to its resistance: V = I * R.
answers.11: Newton's second law states that the net force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration, F = m * a; more generally, force equals the rate of change of momentum.
answers.12: Kinetic energy is proportional to mass and to the square of speed: KE = (1/2) * m * v^2.
answers.13: Power measures the rate at which energy is transferred or work is done, i.e. energy per unit time, measured in watts (1 W = 1 J/s).
answers.14: Density is defined as mass per unit volume: rho = m / V, typically in kg/m^3.
answers.15: Hooke's law relates the restoring force in an elastic body to its extension or deformation: F = -k * x, where k is the spring constant, valid within the elastic limit.
answers.16: Electrical power equals voltage times current: P = V * I (equivalently I^2 * R or V^2 / R).
answers.17: A joule measures energy (equivalently work or heat); one joule is one newton-metre, or one watt-second.
answers.18: Momentum equals mass times velocity: p = m * v. It is a vector quantity in kg*m/s.
answers.19: Revenue equals price multiplied by quantity sold: R = P * Q.
